claim: Every template wraps the attribute in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so projects targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework get generated formatters and resolvers with no `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`. The requirement asks for all generated code to be decorated. Its derived criterion only allows conditional emission where the attribute does not exist. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in .NET Framework 4.0+ and .NET Standard 2.0, and class targets are valid there. The guard therefore drops the attribute on targets that support it, which includes most multi-targeted libraries. Ledger L5 says to follow the requirement.

claim: The guard `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` is wider than it needs to be. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in netstandard2.0 and in every .NET Framework version MessagePack supports (4.0+), and it applies to classes there. Yet the attribute is dropped for every library targeting netstandard2.0 or net4x, which is a large share of consumers. So the requirement 'all generated code is decorated' is not met on those targets. Conditional emission was only justified where the attribute does not exist.
